title: Chess Surgery
reviewNotes: Three branches, 36 exact positions from a complete four-piece Black root. ...Kf7 h5 ...Kg8 h6 ...g6 preserves room for ...Kh5 in front of the pawn; ...g5 draws. The direct ...Kf6 h6 ...gxh6 rook-pawn defense includes an independent representative route to actual stalemate.
transcript: Only a true genius could find the incredible win that black has in this position. You see both players are left with only one pawn each, but the black king is much closer to the pawns. So, it is clear that black is pushing for an advantage. The first move is very intuitive. King to F7 gets closer to the pawn, and if the white king does nothing, the king is simply going to walk in, collect the white pawn, and very easily [music] convert this end game. But, white does have a more resilient way to try and hold back the black king. Pawn to H5. This defends the G6 square. If now the king decides to insist and plays, for example, king to F6, which seems a very logical move, this is actually a draw by force because of H6, a brilliant sacrifice giving up the last pawn that white has. But, actually, if we take this pawn, our only pawn left is an outside passer, which means that if the white king can reach the corner, there's going to be no way for [music] us to ever win this position. If we walk the pawn up, this is eventually going to end up in a stalemate. And some of you might think, "Well, but this is not a problem. After the pawn sacrifice, we can simply ignore it and go pawn to G5 making a run for the promotion." But, actually, this still fails because white is going to push the pawn to H7, threaten to get a queen, and the black king has to stop it. So, after king to G7 and H8 queen, the king is way too far from the pawn, and now the white king is in time to get in front of the pawn. And since the king and the pawn are side by side, and the king cannot get in front of the pawn, there is [music] actually no way >> [snorts] >> to convert this position into a win. So, is this it? Is this position simply a draw? Yes, it is. So, we cannot go up to F6, and we have to find a surprising resource. King to G8, counterintuitively going back rather than forward. But, the idea is clear. We're trying to get to the pawn from this side. And if white tries to walk in, we're actually going to collect the pawn. And this time we are going to be in front of our own pawn. This is winning. But of course, this doesn't seem to make any sense. Can't white still play [music] h6, sacrifice the pawn? But this time we have the option of just ignoring it. But again, if we go pawn to g5, we are going to realize that after the king's march in, we are going to end up in the same position where the king is stuck behind the black pawn. And this is a draw. But we are not in front of this position for no reason. Black does [music] have a win with the ever so patient pawn to g6, only taking one step because of course, we are trying to collect the white pawn. And this time, if the white king marches in, we're going to be able to play king to h5, getting finally in front of the black pawn. And this, with some technique, is going to be a pretty simple conversion into a winning king and pawn ending.
